promise: Compare a behavioral hypothesis with a model prediction—without calling it a real participant.
audience: Researchers and product teams exploring explicit choice and learning hypotheses.
trigger: Use when framing a behavioral simulation, interpreting Centaur output, or planning a comparison against real observations.

modes.name: Frame
modes.when: A behavioral question needs a falsifiable experiment.
modes.output: A choice task, task-domain fit assessment, label counterbalance, and a human-validation gap.

modes.name: Simulate
modes.when: An authorized model endpoint and exact prompt are available.
modes.output: An attributed model prediction with actual probability availability and a reproducible prompt.

modes.name: Compare
modes.output: A preregistered held-out comparison with calibration and domain limits.

examples.title: A preference estimate without a probability
examples.brief: A fictional kiosk team compares two confirmation flows; a backend returns Q with no log-probabilities.
examples.before: The parser reports 100% and the team calls that a customer preference rate.
examples.after: Report choice Q, probability unavailable, exact prompt and backend; counterbalance labels and plan an observed task test before a product decision.
examples.why: A generated choice is not certainty, a participant, or an observed population rate.

boundaries: A model prediction is not real participant evidence, consent, prevalence, or clinical advice.
Centaur serving, licensed weights, compute, endpoint credentials, and domain validation are optional runtime concerns.
The portable method can frame and critique a simulation without any model deployment.

verification.name: Centaur engine regression suite
verification.evidence: 164 tests. Mocked REST/CLI/backend protocol and prompt/result behavior; missing chosen-token probability is null, not 1.0. No Centaur model deployed or inference called.
verification.expected: The stated scope passes; no broader result inferred.

verification.name: Portable packaging and install
verification.command: python3 scripts/capability.py build; python3 scripts/capability.py check; python3 scripts/capability.py doctor; python3 scripts/capability.py install --dest <temporary-parent> (twice)
verification.expected: Byte-identical canonical ZIP and isolated idempotent install.
verification.evidence: All operations passed. No runtime activation or effectiveness measured.

verification.name: Skill discovery metadata
verification.expected: Valid required frontmatter, naming, and complete scaffold.
verification.evidence: Skill is valid. This is a structural check, not a behavioral benchmark.

sources.role: Primary history and engine retained; methods consolidated behind the canonical portable entry.

evidence_summary: 164 mocked engine regression tests cover prompt/result and backend behavior, including missing probabilities. No model deployment or new inference is part of this release, and no human-behavior accuracy claim is established.
publication_status: Installation and evidence scopes are documented below.

marketing.headline: Explore a behavioral hypothesis before the study.
marketing.lead: Frame a choice or learning task, record what a model predicts, and identify the observations needed to trust that prediction. Useful for preparing research questions and comparing explicit alternatives.

benefits.title: Make the question testable
benefits.body: Name the population, task, alternatives and outcome, including the context the simulation leaves out.

benefits.title: Keep the prediction reproducible
benefits.body: Freeze instructions, labels, prior trials, backend identity and analysis before comparing variants.

benefits.title: Know what remains to learn
benefits.body: Separate model choice, available probabilities and actual participant evidence so a synthetic answer stays interpretable.

walkthrough.title: Frame a bounded task
walkthrough.detail: Translate the decision into an explicit choice or sequence and assess its fit to the available model.

walkthrough.title: Run or leave a prepared experiment
walkthrough.detail: Use an authorized compatible endpoint; without one, deliver the exact prompt and blocked inference step.

walkthrough.title: Compare against observations
walkthrough.detail: Check label sensitivity and held-out human data before making a population claim.

use_when: You need to turn a behavioral idea into a precise experiment.
You want to compare alternative prompts or task formulations.
A simulation result needs calibration against observed participant data.
not_for: Replacing people in a usability study or claiming customer preference rates.
Predicting what a named individual will do, or treating absent log-probabilities as certainty.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Cognitive Simulation to frame a fictional kiosk confirmation study. Compare a single confirm button with a review-then-confirm flow. State task fit, counterbalance response labels, prepare exact prompts and define the observed-user check. Do not run an endpoint.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional experiment: kiosk confirmation
Alternatives: confirm / review then confirm
Labels: counterbalanced across variants
Prediction: pending compatible endpoint
Probability: unavailable until returned
Human check: observed errors and task completion under a declared study
marketing.proof_summary: 164 mocked engine regression tests cover prompt/result and backend behavior, including missing probabilities. No model deployment or new inference is part of this release, and no human-behavior accuracy claim is established.
marketing.next_step: Bring the decision, intended population and alternatives you want to compare.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.
